problem: The figure description says the velocity splits into a tangential part and a normal part, and draws edges from 'Velocity v' to a_t and a_n. Velocity never splits: it has no normal component (as Quiz Q2 correctly states). It is the acceleration that splits into a_t and a_n.
fix: Aria: 'The acceleration of a particle splits into a tangential part that changes its speed and a normal part that turns it toward the centre of curvature; the two add as perpendicular vectors to give the total acceleration. The velocity stays along the tangent.' Draw the edges from the acceleration node, not from 'Velocity v'.

problem: The direction formula tan⁻¹(a_n/a_t) is undefined when a_t = 0 (constant-speed motion), the very case used in Q3 and Q5, so a student may be stuck.
fix: Add: when a_t = 0 the angle is 90° from the tangent, i.e. the acceleration is purely normal, pointing to the centre of curvature.

problem: 'r̈ | radial speed change' is imprecise. r̈ is the rate of change of the radial velocity ṙ, not a change of speed; the body text wording 'radial speeding up' has the same looseness.
fix: Table row: 'r̈ | rate of change of radial velocity ṙ'. In the text: 'r̈ is how fast the radial velocity ṙ is changing'.

problem: The remark 'ax = ẍ and ay = ÿ; these are just Cartesian components' belongs to the rectangular-components topic and is dropped in without use; it distracts from the radial-transverse derivation.
fix: Delete the sentence, or replace it with a use: 'Rectangular components are the special case θ = 0, when a_r becomes ẍ and a_θ becomes ÿ.'
